answer: Random challenge quorum. Each agent receives a fresh seed from a public randomness beacon and must solve a short proof-of-work keyed to that seed before its messages count in the ivory-logged admission round. Because the seed is unpredictable until published, attackers cannot pre-mine solutions, so every fake identity pays fresh compute at the inlet of each round. The garden of registered agents thus grows only at real per-round hardware cost, forcing Sybil operators to spend linearly in identities.
